title: Error catalogue — symptom, cause, next step, document
intro: {{ENTRY_COUNT}} entries, each written from a recorded request, not from reading the code alone. Every row resolves to a page anchor, and every `capture_fail` / `capture_fix` id exists in contracts/captures.json, so the catalogue can be re-verified after a code change.

severity_legend.blocker: A published flow cannot complete in production.
severity_legend.high: Silent data loss, wrong money, or an access-control gap.
severity_legend.medium: A caller can trigger a confusing failure or a wrong assumption.
severity_legend.low: Costs time, but the outcome is still correct.

entries.title: Authenticated call answers 请先登录 even though the client sent a token
entries.symptom: Every authenticated request returns 401 请先登录. The token in local storage is valid and the account exists.
entries.cause: The handlers require the header to start with `Bearer ` (server/index.js:312), but the shipped client sends the bare token: `'Authorization': wx.getStorageSync('token')` in utils/api.js:18. The prefix is never added anywhere.
entries.next_step: Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. One-line client fix: `'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + (wx.getStorageSync('token') || '')`. Decide the convention once and document it in the client wrapper, not in each page.
entries.verify: The two captured pairs differ only in the header: capture-fail returns 401 请先登录, capture-fix returns 200 with an empty address list.

entries.title: A badly signed token is reported as an expired session
entries.symptom: A token that was never valid (wrong signature, tampered payload) produces 登录已过期, the same message as a genuinely expired one.
entries.cause: The handler wraps `jwt.verify` in a blanket try/catch (server/index.js:317-326) and maps every error, including JsonWebTokenError, to the expiry message. The global error middleware that distinguishes the two (server/index.js:1397-1403) is never reached because the handler swallows the error first.
entries.next_step: Branch on the error: `TokenExpiredError` → 登录已过期, anything else → 无效的登录凭证. The client can then decide between refresh and re-login instead of guessing.
entries.verify: capture-fail uses a well-formed JWT with a replaced signature and receives 登录已过期, which proves the collapse.

entries.title: Sign-in reveals whether a username exists
entries.symptom: Wrong credentials return one of two different texts: 用户不存在 or 密码错误.
entries.cause: server/index.js:63 and :68 answer separately for a missing account and a wrong password. Combined with no rate limiting anywhere in the service, the pair turns sign-in into a username oracle.
entries.next_step: Return one message for both branches (凭据无效) and keep the specific reason in the server log. Until that ships, do not mirror the distinction in UI copy.
entries.verify: capture-fail and the second 401 pair (login-bad-password) return the two different strings for the same status code.

entries.title: An administrator token passes every user route and reads as an empty account
entries.symptom: With a valid admin token, user endpoints return HTTP 200 and empty payloads. The address list is `[]`, never the addresses that exist.
entries.cause: Only one login exists and it mints `{id, username}` (server/index.js:65). User handlers read `decoded.phone` (server/index.js:321), which is undefined for an admin token, so the filter matches nothing. `jwt.verify` succeeds, so nothing is rejected either.
entries.next_step: Add a user-scoped login that signs `{phone}` and keep the two token audiences apart, for example with a `typ` claim and a check per route family. Treat the empty 200 as a data-loss symptom, not as a normal empty state.
entries.verify: capture-fix sends the admin token with the correct prefix and still returns `{"code":0,"data":[]}`.

entries.title: Any eleven characters are accepted as a phone number
entries.symptom: `abcdefghijk` is accepted and a verification code is issued for it.
entries.cause: The only check is `phone.length !== 11` (server/index.js:264). The `validatePhone` helper with the real `1[3-9]\d{9}` pattern already exists in the same file (server/index.js:34) and is not used here.
entries.next_step: Call the existing helper before issuing a code, and add a per-phone and per-IP throttle; the code store currently has no limit and is never cleaned up.
entries.verify: capture-fail records a 200 for a non-numeric number; the neighbouring seven-character case returns 400, which shows the check is length-only.

entries.title: No SMS is ever sent — the code is printed to the server console
entries.symptom: The API answers 验证码已发送, the user's phone stays silent, and the six digits appear only in the server log.
entries.cause: There is no SMS provider integration. server/index.js:274 does `console.log` with the code; the in-memory store at server/index.js:202 is the only destination.
entries.next_step: Until a provider is wired, do not describe this as sent. In the integrator guide, state plainly that the code is delivered out of band, and add the provider call plus failure handling before any release that depends on it.
entries.verify: Start the service, request a code, and read stdout — the code is the last line. No outbound request is made.

entries.title: Order creation rejects eight fields at once in one joined string
entries.symptom: One 400 response lists every missing field, joined by full-width semicolons, so the client cannot point at a single input.
entries.cause: `validateOrderData` collects all failures into an array and answers `errors.join('；')` (server/index.js:43-53). There is no field key in the response, only prose.
entries.next_step: Parse defensively or, better, validate the same rules client-side before sending. When the endpoint gains an error field map, keep the joined text as `message` for existing callers.
entries.verify: capture-fail sends a body that violates seven of the eight rules and receives all seven reasons in the order they are checked.

entries.title: Two orders created in the same millisecond share an id
entries.symptom: Two order records with the same `id`; later reads return whichever one the lookup finds first.
entries.cause: `id: Date.now().toString()` (server/index.js:87) is the only identifier strategy for orders, addresses, ratings and reviews. Under concurrent submission, or a client retry loop, duplicate keys are reachable.
entries.next_step: Key on a monotonic counter, a UUID, or the order number with its random suffix widened. `order_no` (CK + date + four random digits) is 10 000 values per day, which is better than a millisecond but still not unique.
entries.verify: Send two creations in parallel with `curl --parallel`; compare `data.id`. The capture set cannot show this, because it is a race, so the check is the reproduction above.

entries.title: A stale order id answers 404 with the same envelope as a validation error
entries.symptom: Opening an order from a bookmark returns 404 订单不存在. The client cannot tell this from a malformed request, because both carry `code: -1`.
entries.cause: Only the HTTP status separates the cases (server/index.js:190). The body has no error taxonomy, so any client that reads `code` treats every failure the same.
entries.next_step: Treat 404 as 'remove it from the list' rather than 'show an error', and refresh the list on it. See E-ENVELOPE if you need a machine-readable reason.
entries.verify: capture-fail uses a well-formed but unknown id and receives 404; capture-fix shows the same request with a live id.

entries.title: Assignment answers 请选择工程师 even when the order is also wrong
entries.symptom: A dispatcher sends an assign without an engineer and gets told to pick an engineer, which is correct but hides that the order id was wrong too.
entries.cause: The body is validated before the order is looked up (server/index.js:1030). Failures are reported one at a time, so a request with two problems shows only the first.
entries.next_step: Disable the assign action until an engineer is selected, then treat any remaining 400 as a genuine bug rather than a user error.
entries.verify: capture-fail omits `engineer_id`; capture-fix repeats the same call with the field present and gets 200.

entries.title: An unknown order masks an unknown engineer
entries.symptom: The engineer id in the form is out of date, but the error blames the order.
entries.cause: Checks run body, then order (:1036), then engineer (:1039). Two different failures share one status code and one envelope, so the second is unreachable while the first fails.
entries.next_step: Fix the order id first, then re-run the call to surface the engineer error. When the endpoint gains error codes, give the two 404s different ones so the UI can point at the right field.
entries.verify: capture-fail passes a live engineer against an unknown order and receives 订单不存在 rather than 工程师不存在.

entries.title: Completing an order that is not in progress fails without saying what state it is in
entries.message: 只能完成服务中的订单
entries.symptom: Completion is refused on an order the operator believes is in progress. The message names the required state but not the current one.
entries.cause: The guard compares against `processing` only (server/index.js:1090) and answers with a fixed string. The handler does not echo the current status, so the operator has to reload the detail view to find out.
entries.next_step: Reload the order, confirm the status, and drive it to `processing` (confirm, then start, or assign) before completing. Prefer showing the current status in the UI rather than relying on the message.
entries.verify: capture-fail completes a `pending` order and is refused; capture-fix completes the same order after assignment, when it is `processing`.

entries.title: Starting a pending order is refused because confirm was skipped
entries.message: 只能开始已确认的订单
entries.symptom: Start is refused on a freshly created order. The operator sees no reason in the message for the missing step.
entries.cause: `start` requires `confirmed` (server/index.js:1065), while `assign` jumps straight to `processing` without confirming. Two routes reach `processing`, and only one of them needs the confirm step, which makes the required sequence inconsistent.
entries.next_step: Choose one path and document it. Today: assign (which forces `processing`) or confirm then start. Do not mix them in one workflow.
entries.verify: capture-fail starts a `pending` order; confirm-ok then start-ok show the two-step path succeeding.

entries.title: The payable amount is taken from the client and never recomputed
entries.symptom: A request for twelve rentals at ¥899 each, submitted with `totalAmount: 0.01`, is accepted and a payment for one fen is prepared.
entries.cause: `totalAmount` is copied from the body into the order and into `total_fee` (server/index.js:1624, :1657). The product records are never consulted, so nothing ties the charge to the catalogue price.
entries.next_step: Recompute the amount server-side from `items[].productId` and the product price, and reject a body whose `totalAmount` disagrees. Do not deploy a payment path that trusts the client for money.
entries.verify: capture-fail is the one-fen request and returns 200 with a workable pay signature.

entries.title: The payment callback rejects every notification, including correctly signed ones
entries.symptom: Every callback from the payment platform is answered `return_code=FAIL`, `return_msg=签名错误`, so an order never becomes paid through the callback.
entries.cause: `bodyParser.json()` is registered globally (server/index.js:14) and there is no XML parser. `req.body` is `{}` for `application/xml`, so `parseXML` (:1688) yields no parameters, `sign` is undefined, and `verifySign` (:1694) cannot succeed. The failure is silent because HTTP is still 200.
entries.next_step: Register a text or raw parser for `application/xml` before the route, and confirm with a captured round trip. Until then, reconcile payments with `GET /api/wxpay/order/:orderNo`, which does flip the status.
entries.verify: capture-fail carries a signature computed exactly as the platform requires (sorted pairs, `&key=`, MD5 upper-case) and is still refused, which isolates the cause to body parsing rather than to the signing code.

entries.title: A plausible path is swallowed by a neighbouring route
entries.symptom: `GET /api/reviews/pending` answers 404 评价不存在. The review queue is not missing — the path resolved to the single-review handler with `id` = `pending`.
entries.cause: No route answers `/api/reviews/pending`, and `/api/reviews/:id` has no guard on the shape of `:id`, so the parameterised route takes it and the lookup fails. The message therefore comes from server/index.js:1533, not from the catch-all at :1772. The real queue is mounted at `/api/admin/reviews/pending`.
entries.next_step: Use the mounted path. When a 404 names a different resource than the URL implies, suspect a routing collision rather than missing data: ask `shyzctl endpoints --grep reviews` instead of guessing a path.
entries.verify: capture-fail is the swallowed path and answers 评价不存在; capture-fix is the mounted path and returns the queue.

entries.title: There is no error taxonomy: `code` is always 0 or -1
entries.symptom: Every failure looks identical to a program: `{"code":-1,"message":"…"}`. Clients branch on the HTTP status, or worse, on the Chinese string.
entries.cause: The success path uses `code: 0`, every failure uses `code: -1` ({{MESSAGE_COUNT}} distinct message strings, one code). No error code, no field name, no request id — so a client cannot react to `库存不足` differently from `订单不存在` without string matching.
entries.next_step: Introduce stable codes such as `ORDER_NOT_FOUND`, keep `message` for humans, and add `field` where validation failed. Version the change by adding fields, never by changing existing strings.
entries.verify: `shyzctl endpoints --json` lists the status codes per endpoint; `shyzctl show POST /api/orders` shows the single `code` value used for eight different validation failures.
